name: Medici
summary: Auction game where merchant houses bid florins for lots of commodity cards to load ships and earn payouts.
rules_text: Medici is played over 3 days. Set up a face-down commodity deck, adjusting size by player count, and give each player 30-40 florins and a ship for 5 cards (7 in 2p). Each turn the active player draws 1 to 3 cards face-up as a single lot, stopping at will up to 3. The lot is then auctioned: each other player in clockwise order may make one increasing bid or pass, the drawer bids last. Minimum bid is 1 and you cannot bid more than your current florins. Winner pays by decreasing money and loads the whole lot on his ship; lots cannot be split or discarded after purchase and you may not bid if the lot would overfill your ship. If all pass, the lot is discarded. When a ship is full that player sits out the rest of the day. Day ends when all but one ship are full, last player fills free from deck, or deck empties. Score ships by value and by commodity track progress, awarding florins, then start next day. Most florins after day 3 wins.
rating_reason: auction bidding for goods fits numeric bids bluffing
